item.title: 23 patients waiting on trolleys in University Hospital Kerry
item.description: There are 23 patients waiting on trolleys in University Hospital Kerry today. That’s according to figures from the Irish Nurses’ and Midwives’ Organisation. They show there are 16 patients waiting on a trolley in UHK’s emergency department, while a further seven people are waiting on trolleys in wards within the hospital. item.title: Killorglin-based energy efficiency company wins National Retrofit Award
item.description: A Killorglin-based company has won a National Retrofit Award. Energy efficiency specialists Retrofit Design Ltd have been named Business All-Star All Ireland Champion Retrofit Company 2026. It is the second year in a row they has won a national award. Advertisement General Manager Chris Scanlon said the award is a reflection of the company’s commitment to quality and customer care.

item.title: Celtic legend passes away
item.description: Celtic legend John 'Dixie' Deans has died aged 79. The former Scotland striker scored 124 goals in 184 games for the Glasgow club, including hat-tricks in the 1972 Scottish Cup and 1974 League Cup finals. Deans was nicknamed Dixie after former England and Everton striker Dixie Dean, due to his goalscoring exploits. Advertisement He hit 89 goals in 198 appearances for Motherwell.

item.title: Details confirmed for All-Ireland semi-finals
item.description: The details have been confirmed for the All-Ireland club senior hurling semi-finals later this month. Leinster champions St Martin's will face Munster kingpins Ballygunner at Semple Stadium in Thurles. While Parnell Park will host the meeting of Ulster's Slaughtneil and Loughrea of Connacht. Advertisement Both final-four clashes are scheduled for Sunday December 21st.

item.title: 2nd Irish swimmer signs for Enhanced Games
item.description: A second Irish swimmer has confirmed they have signed for the Enhanced Games. Paris Olympian Max McCusker will join Shane Ryan at the event, in which athletes are allowed to use performance-enhancing drugs under medical supervision. McCusker compete in the 4-by-100 metres medley relay in Paris last summer, and holds the national records in the 50-metres and 100-metres butterfly. Advertisement

item.title: Helmut Marko leaves Red Bull
item.description: Red Bull motorsport consultant Helmut Marko has stepped down from his role with the Formula One team. The 82-year-old Austrian former racing driver has overseen the rise of some of the sport's stars over the past two decades, including four-time champions Max Verstappen and Sebastian Vettel. He says he's filled with "pride" and wishes Red Bull "continued success". Advertisement

item.title: Four Kerry entities forced to pay almost €1 million to the Revenue Commissioners in latest list
item.description: Four Kerry entities have been forced to pay almost €1 million (€964,363) to the Revenue Commissioners. They were included in the most recent List of Tax Defaulters, published by Revenue this afternoon. The list covers the period 1 July to 30 September 2025. item.title: Health watchdog finds significant building defects at Killarney Community Hospital
item.description: The health watchdog found significant building defects in a HSE centre for older people in Killarney. The Health Information and Quality Authority carried out an unannounced inspection at Killarney Community Hospital in September, and has published the report from that inspection. The centre for older people on St Margaret’s Road, operated by the HSE, has capacity for 66 residents. item.title: An Ghaeltacht chairman says they're in privileged position
item.description: An Ghaeltacht chairman Dara O'Cinneide says it's a privileged position to be in as they prepare for an All-Ireland Intermediate Club Football Championship semi-final. The Munster champions will this coming Sunday discover whether they're to go up against Tubberclair of Westmeath or Kildare's Sallins over the first weekend of next month. An Ghaeltacht took their own provincial honours by overcoming Aghabullogue 2-12 to 1-8. Advertisement O'Cinneide is full of praise for everyone involved

item.title: Ferguson loan spell at Roma set to end
item.description: Republic of Ireland striker Evan Ferguson could see his loan spell at Roma come to a premature end this January. Italian media report that the Serie A club are hoping to return Ferguson to his parent club Brighton. Ferguson has made 14 appearances and scored one goal since arriving in the Italian capital this summer on a loan move. Advertisement
